lines: This page studies how ordinary letters can carry a second visual structure while remaining
readable text. A reader should be able to follow each sentence at its normal size. A camera sees
the same letters as a pattern of light and dark marks. Those two views need to agree before the
experiment can be useful. The shape of a letter depends on its font, its size, and the space around
it. A small change in line spacing can affect a scanner without changing the words. Different
readers also process an image in different ways. One successful result does not tell us how every
phone will behave. We preserve the original text and record every test, including failures. The
goal is a page that remains clear to a person and works with an ordinary reader. A separate image
export can be useful, but it does not prove that text will keep its layout in another application.
